title: arxiv_2007.06344v1
universal_lens: The transition from discrete tracking-by-detection to continuous global response maps establishes a topological isomorphism between spatiotemporal object trajectories and differentiable manifolds. By replacing hard bounding boxes with Gaussian-like probability distributions, the system unifies detection and association into a single end-to-end optimization over a unified latent state space. The proposed framework unifies spatiotemporal tracking via a global response manifold. By mapping discrete bounding boxes to continuous Gaussian distributions, the system formulates object persistence as a logical inference over temporal windows, seamlessly integrating motion displacement regression into an end-to-end differentiable state-transition operator.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the global response map as a conformal Bayesian posterior over player presence. The motion displacement regressor acts as a dynamic prior, updating belief states across frames. This allows robust inference of occluded athletes by maintaining positive probabilistic responses despite missing visual data. GSI maps the local response map generation to a Bayesian posterior density estimation. The logical inference methodology acts as a conformal prediction set under heavy occlusion, ensuring that unseen targets maintain calibrated probability bounds across time steps without relying on explicit appearance feature metric learning.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the end-to-end framework models situational reasoning via continuous state transitions. Object locating defines spatial priors, while displacement regression calculates instantaneous velocity vectors. Data linking executes optimal assignment without combinatorial explosion, enabling real-time tactical state updates during complex multi-agent interactions. In GSE, the Global Response Map functions as the situational awareness layer. Motion displacement regression provides the Markovian state-transition kernel for player trajectories, while the logical inference mechanism dynamically updates entity existence probabilities during complex defensive occlusions and spatial interactions.

primitives.name: Tracking-by-Detection Paradigm Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Most existing Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) approaches follow the Tracking-by-Detection paradigm and the data association framework where objects are firstly detected and then associated.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: D_t: Set of detections at time t (dimensionless), A_{t,t+1}: Association matrix mapping D_t to D_{t+1} (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes independent detection events and Markovian state transitions; relies on high precision of isolated frame detectors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails under severe occlusion or rapid illumination changes where detection recall drops below critical thresholds, causing identity switches.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to traditional two-stage sports analytics pipelines where ball/player detection precedes trajectory stitching.
layer2.telemetry: ID Switches (IDS) and Mostly Tracked (MT) rates.

primitives.name: Global Response Map Generator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Specifically, with our introduced multi-object representation strategy, a global response map can be accurately generated over frames, from which the trajectory of each tracked object can be easily picked up, just like how a detector inputs an image and outputs the bounding boxes of each detected object.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: R(x,y,t): Global response intensity at spatial coordinates (x,y) in meters at time t (dimensionless, range [0,1]).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes object presence can be modeled as a smooth, localized peak within the continuous spatial domain.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates when multiple objects overlap perfectly, causing peak merging that prevents distinct trajectory extraction.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's heat-map generation for player positioning, replacing discrete bounding boxes with continuous probability fields.
layer2.telemetry: Peak localization error (pixels/meters) and MOTA score.

primitives.name: Motion Displacement Regressor
primitives.verbatim_quote: To address the problem, we present a completely end-to-end approach that takes imagesequence/video as input and outputs directly the located and tracked objects of learned types.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Delta x, \Delta y: Spatial displacement components between consecutive frames (meters/frame).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes quasi-constant velocity or smooth acceleration dynamics between adjacent video frames.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities occur during instantaneous direction changes or collisions where velocity vectors become discontinuous.

layer2.mapping: Functions identically to optical flow networks in GSE, predicting next-state spatial coordinates to resolve ambiguous assignments.
layer2.telemetry: Velocity estimation RMSE and assignment accuracy.

primitives.name: MOT Challenge Formulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: There are three key issues that a MOT framework should handle: 1) Modeling the dynamic motion of multiple objects; 2) Handling the entering/exiting of objects into/from the scene; 3) Robustness against occlusion and appearance/background variations.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: N(t): Number of active objects at time t (integer), O_c: Occlusion mask (boolean).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes the underlying physical system obeys deterministic kinematics perturbed by stochastic observation noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in highly cluttered environments with dense, indistinguishable agents moving in synchronized patterns.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to GSE boundary conditions: handling substitutions (entering/exiting) and defensive screens (occlusions).
layer2.telemetry: False Positives (FP) and False Negatives (FN) counts.

primitives.name: Logical Inference Occlusion Handler
primitives.verbatim_quote: Differently, in our work, the occlusion problem is well handled by considering a window of frames to locate objects with an introduced logical inference methodology, without explicit appearance feature for metric learning.

reasoning_traces.think: The foundational shift proposed in this chapter window represents a profound epistemic transition from discrete, modular perception to continuous, holistic state estimation. Historically, Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) has been shackled to the 'Tracking-by-Detection' paradigm, treating object existence as a series of binary, isolated events constrained by rigid bounding boxes. This modular approach inherently fragments the temporal continuity of an agent's existence, creating a combinatorial nightmare during data association when detections fail due to occlusion or blur. The authors dismantle this fragmented ontology by introducing the Global Response Map (GRM). Mathematically, the GRM elevates the representation of an object from a discrete set of vertices (bounding box corners) to a continuous, differentiable scalar field over the spatiotemporal manifold. In this new topology, an object is not a static entity but a persistent, Gaussian-like probability distribution that evolves smoothly across frames. This continuous embedding naturally absorbs the uncertainties inherent in visual data; even if pixel-level features are obscured, the momentum of the probability distribution maintains the object's 'presence'. Furthermore, by integrating a motion displacement regressor—functionally analogous to an optical flow network—the system explicitly models the derivative of this field, capturing the dynamic velocity vector of each agent. This eliminates the need for heuristic, post-hoc assignment algorithms (like Hungarian matching on IoU) because the trajectory emerges intrinsically from the peaks of the evolving response map. Consequently, the entire pipeline becomes a single, end-to-end differentiable function, optimizing detection, association, and motion prediction simultaneously. This unification drastically reduces computational overhead while enhancing robustness, offering a mathematically elegant solution to the chaotic, high-uncertainty environments typical of real-world scenarios.

Just as a coach anticipates a player's path based on momentum rather than relying solely on current visibility, the network predicts future states by regressing motion displacements, effectively simulating the intent and inertia of the tracked entities.

Additionally, if the motion displacement regressor outputs vectors violating physical constraints (e.g., superluminal speeds or impossible accelerations relative to the sport's biomechanics), the layer must reject the prediction to prevent cascading hallucinations in the trajectory.

The mathematical foundation of this chapter window rests on the paradigm shift from discrete, fragmented tracking-by-detection pipelines to a holistic, end-to-end differentiable manifold. Historically, multi-object tracking (MOT) suffered from error propagation due to decoupled detection and association modules. The authors introduce a Global Response Map (GRM) which fundamentally alters the state space representation. Instead of treating bounding boxes as isolated entities, they are mapped to continuous Gaussian distributions (Equation 1-3). This creates a saliency landscape where object presence is a scalar field $z \in [0,1]$. 

The derivation hinges on two critical innovations: the geometric parameterization of the Gaussian radius $r$ and variance $\sigma$, and the Logical Inference Methodology. The former ensures that the spatial footprint of an object is smoothly integrated into the network's loss function, allowing gradient flow from the final assignment back to the initial localization. The latter addresses the fundamental epistemic gap in visual tracking: the absence of evidence is not evidence of absence. By utilizing a temporal window of history states, the GRM infers the latent state of occluded objects without relying on brittle appearance features. 

This is mathematically unified through the Motion Displacement Regression sub-network. Rather than computationally expensive iterative ROI cropping, the network takes the center point distributions retrieved from the GRM (post-NMS) and directly regresses the motion dynamics. This forms a cohesive Markovian transition model embedded within a deep neural architecture. The resulting framework elegantly bypasses the need for explicit hand-crafted metrics, leveraging the implicit metric learning of the end-to-end structure to handle complex interactions, thereby establishing a robust primitive for high-dimensional state estimation in dynamic environments.

If the motion displacement network inadvertently learns to rely on static background cues rather than true object dynamics, the system will fail during camera pans. Furthermore, anti-collinearity checks are required to ensure the logical inference window does not simply memorize training sequence lengths, which would catastrophically break generalization on varying frame rates.
